articles.title: A Generalized Sparse Fuzzy Clustering Framework with Automated Cluster Cardinality Estimation Ability
articles.raw_summary: Fuzzy clustering provides a robust framework for handling ambiguous and overlapping data boundaries, yet its traditional formulation generates entirely dense membership assignments that limit noise resilience and prevent estimating the true number of clusters, when it is unknown. articles.title: Learning to bid and bundle: a posterior-sampling agent for online retail
articles.raw_summary: An online retailer launching a perishable product bids for sponsored-search clicks, discounts a bundle with an always-stocked staple and displays its remaining stock, which raises willingness to pay. It knows neither how clicks respond to its bid nor how strong and dispersed its market is, and learns both over repeated seasons from data its own decisions censor: a zero bid reveals nothing about paid clicks, and choices follow only clicks. articles.title: Early Stopping in Large Reasoning Models: A Survey and Empirical Audit of Efficiency and Reliability
articles.raw_summary: Large reasoning models can improve accuracy by generating longer reasoning traces, but some of this computation may be unnecessary. Early-stopping methods aim to stop once enough reasoning is available to answer. Evaluating these methods requires accounting for the cost of deciding when to stop and the reliability of the resulting answer. We evaluate different methods across five reasoning models on mathematical and scientific reasoning, code generation, and factuality tasks by using a shared rollout replay protocol. We introduce Target-Integrated Token Efficiency (TITE) to measure efficiency

articles.title: FB-MOAC: A Reinforcement Learning Algorithm for Forward-Backward Markov Decision Processes
articles.raw_summary:
Reinforcement learning (RL) algorithms are effective in solving problems that can be modeled as Markov decision processes (MDPs).
  These algorithms primarily target forward MDPs whose dynamics evolve over time from an initial state.
  However, several important problems in different scenarios including stochastic control and network systems exhibit both a forward and a backward dynamics. As a consequence, they cannot be expressed as a standard MDP, thereby calling
  for a novel theory for RL in this context.

articles.title: Interpretable structural temperature scaling for calibrating graph neural networks and point-cloud segmentation
articles.raw_summary: Graph-aware calibrators make graph neural networks (GNNs) more trustworthy by predicting a temperature for each node, usually with auxiliary networks whose decisions are hard to inspect. We propose Interpretable Structural Temperature Scaling (ISTS), a twelve-parameter linear model that sets each node's temperature from named descriptors of its confidence, neighbourhood and closeness to labelled nodes, so every temperature traces back to descriptor contributions. articles.title: ProLand: A New Infeasible Manifold Optimization Method for LoRA Fine-Tuning
articles.raw_summary: Low-rank adaptation (LoRA) enables parameter-efficient fine-tuning but can suffer from redundant basis directions.
